kallander-field-repairs.description: Scoping, vendor pricing, and DPW coordination for repairing turf and playing surface conditions at Kallander Field.
kallander-field-repairs.status: Turf repairs at Kallander Field remain under review after original contractor North Turf provided an $8,000 to $9,000 estimate in May 2026. The proposed repair, coordinated with Department of Public Works materials, falls well within the Recreation Commission's remaining capital balance of $13,000 to $14,000. No board has taken a formal position, and a presentation and decision originally targeted for June have not yet occurred.

kratom-retail-ban.name: Statewide kratom ban and local enforcement
kratom-retail-ban.description: Local Board of Health enforcement and retail monitoring following the state's Schedule I temporary ban on kratom.
kratom-retail-ban.status: Southborough health staff have reviewed local stores following the state's one-year temporary Schedule I classification of kratom, which took effect in August 2026. Only one Southborough retailer was found carrying kratom products, and staff provided guidance on securing, returning, or lawfully disposing of remaining inventory. The Board of Health received the update in September 2026, with no further local board action required.

landfill-environmental-assessment.name: Southborough landfill environmental assessment
landfill-environmental-assessment.description: Environmental risk assessment, private well testing, and potential municipal water line extension regarding contamination from the Southborough landfill.
landfill-environmental-assessment.status: Article 7 heads to Special Town Meeting with unified board support, seeking $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend the town water main and connect two homes near the capped Parkerville Road landfill. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee recommend approval after confirming the town will cover the entire connection cost from the street into the private residences. The project is designed to permanently address contamination risks and avoid perpetual state-mandated well testing following chemical detections in nearby monitoring wells.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on Oct 6 to recommend Article 7 after confirming the town will cover the complete connection costs into the private homes.
Voted 4-0-1 on Sep 15 to recommend Article 7 to eliminate perpetual private well testing mandates and long-term contamination risks.

latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.name: Latisquama Road errant golf balls
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.description: Safety concerns and mitigation options regarding errant golf balls striking residential properties on Latisquama Road from the Southborough Golf Club.
latisquama-road-errant-golf-balls.status: The Golf Committee is evaluating mitigation options to address errant golf balls from the Southborough Golf Club striking homes on Latisquama Road. Members are considering whether to move the 7th tee box, reorient the green, or convert the hole into a par 3 after prior netting and relocations failed to resolve property damage. The committee intends to consult the course architect on hole redesign options as a standing agenda item.

positions.detail: Seeking recommendations from the golf architect on redesigning the 7th hole following neighborhood reports of significant property damage.

library-book-drop-repair.name: Library book drop concrete repair
library-book-drop-repair.description: Repair and funding of damaged concrete beneath the Southborough Library book drop and clarification of municipal maintenance responsibilities.
library-book-drop-repair.status: The Library Board of Trustees approved replacing the damaged concrete pad beneath the book drop for under $5,000 using library State Aid funds. In response to recurring disputes over whether the Department of Public Works or the library oversees exterior property upkeep, the trustees also voted to send a letter to town officials to clarify maintenance responsibilities. Work was scheduled for early October 2026.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 11, 2026 to fund the pad replacement using State Aid and to draft a letter clarifying DPW and library maintenance duties.

library-cpa-signage.name: Library CPA commemorative signage
library-cpa-signage.description: Design and wording of commemorative plaques crediting Community Preservation Act funding for Southborough Library restoration projects.
library-cpa-signage.status: The Community Preservation Committee approved two commemorative plaques in July 2026 to close out past grants, agreeing to the Library Trustees' preferred wording thanking the 'residents' of Southborough rather than taxpayers or citizens. The bronze plaques, which feature the official town seal, recognize funding for the library's facade restoration and local history preservation. The signs have been commissioned, and invoices have been submitted to the CPC for payment.

positions.detail: Advocated for plaque language crediting Southborough 'residents,' commissioned the signs, and submitted invoices to the CPC for reimbursement.
Voted 5-1 on July 21, 2026, to approve the plaques crediting residents, over one member's preference for 'taxpayers' to recognize business contributions.

library-hotspot-lending-policy.name: Library wireless hotspot lending policy
library-hotspot-lending-policy.description: Policy revisions and fee structures for circulating mobile Wi-Fi hotspots borrowed from the Southborough Library.
library-hotspot-lending-policy.status: The Library Board of Trustees unanimously approved the revised circulating wireless hotspot lending policy on September 14, 2026. The updated rules mandate direct in-person returns to staff, establish a $15 replacement fee for lost or unreturned chargers directed to the town general fund, and allow six-month borrowing suspensions for repeat violations. No further board approvals or hearings are required.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Sep 14 to adopt the revised hotspot lending rules, charger replacement fees, and suspension terms.

library-parking-lot-repaving.name: Library parking lot repaving
library-parking-lot-repaving.description: Capital planning, DPW coordination, and town warrant sponsorship for repaving the Southborough Library parking lot.
library-parking-lot-repaving.status: Repaving of the Southborough Library parking lot has been deferred and will not be submitted as a capital request for FY28. Site engineering requirements to manage runoff and protect the water table added granite features that drove up costs beyond what could be funded near-term or covered by library state aid. The project is instead slated to be proposed for town capital planning in two to three years.

positions.detail: Agreed to defer the capital repaving request for two to three years due to elevated engineering costs for drainage and water table protection.

library-security-cameras.name: Library security camera installation
library-security-cameras.description: Procurement, State Aid funding, and contract liability terms for additional security cameras at the Southborough Library.
library-security-cameras.status: The Library Board of Trustees provisionally approved a $6,775 contract with Custom Alarm to install three to four additional security cameras in the library basement, Eaton Room, and children's room emergency exit, funded through the State Aid account. The approval is subject to Town Counsel's review of vendor contract clauses that limit liability and require town indemnification. Final judgment on whether to proceed following legal review rests with the library director.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on March 9, 2026, to approve the contract pending Town Counsel review, despite one member's objection to vendor liability and indemnification terms.

lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.name: Lynbrook Road water main rehabilitation
lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.description: Notice of Intent and cured-in-place structural lining of an aging 12-inch water main along I-495 and Lynbrook Road.
lynbrook-road-water-main-rehabilitation.status: The Conservation Commission unanimously approved an Order of Conditions in April 2026 for the rehabilitation of an aging 12-inch water main along Lynbrook Road using cured-in-place pipe lining. The Department of Public Works is coordinating the project ahead of state repaving and the planned transfer of Lynbrook Road from MassDOT to the town. Prior to construction, the contractor must submit final design plans and dewatering protocols for review and approval.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 2, 2026, to approve an Order of Conditions with requirements for pre-construction design and dewatering submittals.

masc-calendar-study-resolution.name: MASC statewide school calendar study resolution
masc-calendar-study-resolution.description: Resolution sponsored through the Massachusetts Association of School Committees seeking a state study on school calendar configurations.
masc-calendar-study-resolution.status: The combined school committees deferred action in March 2026 on sponsoring a Massachusetts Association of School Committees (MASC) resolution requesting a state study of school calendar configurations. Members directed that an explanatory preamble be drafted to clarify that the study would gather comparative data on statutory requirements, vacations, and religious observances rather than mandate local schedule changes. No further action or committee votes have been recorded ahead of or following MASC's June 2026 submission deadline.

positions.body: Northborough, Southborough, and Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committees
positions.detail: Deferred taking a formal vote in March 2026 to allow drafting of a preamble clarifying that the resolution seeks statewide data collection rather than mandated local calendar changes.

mbta-communities-zoning-correction.name: MBTA Communities zoning table correction
mbta-communities-zoning-correction.description: Town Meeting warrant article to correct transcription errors in the MBTA Communities Overlay District dimensional table.
mbta-communities-zoning-correction.status: Town Meeting approved Article 31 on April 11, 2026, adopting the clerical corrections to the MBTA Communities Overlay District dimensional table. The housekeeping amendment replaced an errant word with a comma across three columns and removed a typographical percent symbol from the floor area ratio value. The measure took effect without altering underlying zoning or development standards.

positions.detail: Brought forward the article as a noncontroversial housekeeping correction to fix typographical transcription errors.
Voted on April 11, 2026, to pass Article 31.

mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.name: McAuliffe Hearing Room audiovisual upgrades
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.description: Hardware, camera framing, and video conferencing upgrades for hybrid public meetings in the McAuliffe Hearing Room at the Town House.
mcauliffe-hearing-room-av.status: Audiovisual upgrades in the McAuliffe Hearing Room have been installed and are undergoing ongoing fine-tuning. Recent adjustments included lowering front desk monitors to improve audience sightlines, though microphone calibration and displaying remote participant lists in the room remain active issues. The Municipal Technology Committee is continuing to track feedback and oversee remaining technical configurations.

positions.detail: Overseeing the rollout and troubleshooting of the new displays, cameras, and audio equipment, and continuing to monitor user feedback.

metrowest-recc-borrowing.name: MetroWest RECC borrowing authorization
metrowest-recc-borrowing.description: Short-term borrowing authorization of up to $12.5 million to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center.
metrowest-recc-borrowing.status: The Select Board approved up to $12.5 million in short-term borrowing in May 2026 to bridge state grant funding for the MetroWest Regional Emergency Communication Center. The vote followed matching approvals by partner communities Grafton and Westborough, though one board member opposed Southborough assuming borrowing risk for the regional district. A resident also raised concerns regarding potential municipal liability for non-reimbursable facility costs. No further local board action is currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on May 19, 2026, to authorize the bridge financing, with one member opposed over concerns about taking on borrowing risk for the regional district.
A resident expressed concern over town liability for non-reimbursable lease, legal, and insurance expenses, urging public disclosure of all financial agreements.

multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.name: Multi-year road and sidewalk borrowing
multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.description: Proposed multi-million dollar capital borrowing authorization and debt exclusion for comprehensive road and sidewalk improvements.
multi-year-road-and-sidewalk-borrowing.status: Town Meeting approved a 20-year, $25 million capital borrowing authorization under Article 13 in April 2026 to fund a comprehensive five-year road pavement plan and four new sidewalks. The Select Board backed the measure and placed a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion question on the May 2026 Annual Town Election ballot, which town officials noted is required for the borrowing to take effect. No subsequent action or election results appear in the record.

positions.detail: Approved Article 13 by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, authorizing $25 million in borrowing for road repairs and sidewalk construction.
Voted 4-0-1 on April 7 to recommend Article 13, shifting from an earlier 3-2 split, and voted 5-0 to place the debt exclusion on the ballot.
Voted on March 18 to hold its recommendation until Town Meeting, citing concerns about authorizing up to $25 million without a detailed cash flow and rollout schedule.
Requested a Town Meeting floor amendment requiring MassDOT invasive plant management guidelines and weed-free soil, which was defeated.
Residents spoke in favor of the borrowing, citing pothole hazards, narrow roads lacking sidewalks, and professional engineering support for the pavement plan.

municipal-financial-policies.name: Municipal financial policies adoption
municipal-financial-policies.description: Review and formal adoption of town financial policies recommended by the Massachusetts Division of Local Services.
municipal-financial-policies.status: Adoption of the town's comprehensive municipal financial policies is largely stalled following the approval of six individual policies earlier this year. The Select Board previously shelved recommended state reserve policies because the town cannot meet the reserve levels, and it placed budget development policies on hold pending clarification from town counsel and state officials. Most recently, on October 6, the board tabled the draft procurement and conflict of interest policy indefinitely, criticizing it as overly rigid and redundant with state ethics laws.

positions.detail: Has adopted six financial policies, but shelved the reserve policy and indefinitely tabled the procurement and ethics policy due to burdensome contractor requirements.

municipal-grants-management-policy.name: Municipal Grants Management Policy
municipal-grants-management-policy.description: Town oversight and approval procedures governing municipal grant applications, match funding, and operational liabilities.
municipal-grants-management-policy.status: The Select Board unanimously approved the amended Grants Management Financial Policy in April 2026. The policy sets town oversight and approval procedures for municipal grant applications, matching funds, and operational liabilities. No further board review or action is currently pending.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Apr 28, 2026, to approve the Grants Management Financial Policy as amended.

municipal-health-insurance-reform.name: Municipal employee health insurance reform
municipal-health-insurance-reform.description: Adoption of MGL Chapter 32B Sections 21-23 and collective bargaining with the Public Employee Committee to modify municipal health insurance plans.
municipal-health-insurance-reform.status: The Select Board voted to accept Massachusetts General Law Chapter 32B, Sections 21 through 23, authorizing expedited collective negotiations with the Public Employee Committee over municipal health insurance plan designs. The decision aligns Southborough with Northborough and the regional school district to pursue coordinated changes to reduce premium expenses, which represent 11.2 percent of the town budget. Formal negotiations with employee representatives are expected to follow, targeting plan modifications that would take effect July 1, 2027.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Aug 11 to adopt MGL Chapter 32B, Sections 21-23, to pursue coordinated negotiations with the Public Employee Committee to reduce health insurance costs.

municipal-phone-system-upgrade.name: Municipal phone system upgrade
municipal-phone-system-upgrade.description: Capital request and transition of municipal facilities from an unsupported on-premise PBX phone system to a cloud-based solution.
municipal-phone-system-upgrade.status: The Municipal Technology Committee voted unanimously in March 2026 to support a $25,000 Annual Town Meeting capital request to replace the town's aging on-premise PBX system with a cloud-based phone network. The project is intended to cover all municipal departments, including public safety, and would carry an estimated $32,000 to $33,000 in annual operating costs. No further action or vote on the capital request is recorded.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Mar 3, 2026, to recommend the $25,000 capital request, citing unsupported user licenses and risk of hardware failures in the current 15-year-old system.

national-grid-vegetation-plan.name: National Grid FY27 vegetation management plan
national-grid-vegetation-plan.description: Annual review and approval of National Grid's tree pruning and vegetation management plan along town distribution circuits.
national-grid-vegetation-plan.status: National Grid's fiscal year 2027 vegetation management plan is approved following a joint review by the Planning Board and town tree warden in August 2026. The work covers routine clearance pruning along distribution circuits on Parmenter Road, Pine Hill Road, Nichols Street, and Clemmons Street, with no full tree removals included in the routine scope. Any hazardous tree removals will be handled separately through joint hearings.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on August 17 to approve the annual vegetation management plan.
Concurred with the Planning Board on August 17 to approve the utility's pruning plan.
A resident questioned utility clearance standards versus town standards and raised concerns about the aesthetic impact of roadside tree trimming.

native-plant-landscape-regulations.name: Native plant landscape regulations
native-plant-landscape-regulations.description: Proposed Planning Board site plan rules and regulations mandating native plantings and invasive species management.
native-plant-landscape-regulations.status: The Planning Board unanimously adopted new Native Landscape Regulations for site plan review in May 2026. The regulations require 100 percent of new vegetation in site plan review projects to consist of native New England species and ban systemic neonicotinoid pesticides. A separate proposal addressing broader invasive species management was deferred for future study.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on May 11, 2026, to adopt the native planting and pesticide regulations as amended.
Drafted and presented the policy to require native plantings, pollinator habitat, and pesticide bans in site plan reviews.

neary-school-building-project.name: Neary School building project
neary-school-building-project.description: Feasibility, design, and renovation or replacement planning for Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-building-project.status: The Elementary School Building Committee is advancing a roughly $38 million addition and renovation plan (Option 3) after finding that a $15 million baseline upgrade fails to cover essential HVAC, mechanical, and educational needs. The Southborough School Committee has also endorsed addition and renovation as its preferred path, while keeping open the option to submit a Massachusetts School Building Authority Statement of Interest in November that would restart a five- to six-year state funding process. Municipal boards, including the Select Board, Advisory Committee, and Capital Improvement and Planning Committee, plan to convene jointly before Thanksgiving to assess the town's debt capacity for major school projects. The building committee meets October 21, 2026, to formally authorize schematic design work leading toward a targeted March 2027 Town Meeting funding vote.

positions.detail: Supports advancing a roughly $38 million addition and renovation plan (Option 3) after concluding a $15 million baseline upgrade would be consumed by mandatory code work without addressing core building systems.
Voted that an addition and renovation plan is its preferred direction, and plans to deliberate in November on whether to reapply for MSBA state funding.

Residents urged officials to evaluate Neary's costs in the context of town-wide capital demands—including future maintenance at Finn School—and to account for expenses related to relocating district central administration.

neary-school-building-project.next: Elementary School Building Committee vote on schematic design directives on October 21, 2026

neary-school-roof-replacement.name: Neary School roof replacement
neary-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed borrowing and debt exclusion to replace the failing roof and fund ADA upgrades at Neary Elementary School.
neary-school-roof-replacement.status: The Neary Elementary School roof replacement is nearly 90 percent complete, on schedule, and running significantly under budget. The school district expects final demobilization by mid-November 2026 and anticipates returning nearly $2 million of the $4.5 million Town Meeting borrowing appropriation to the town. Standalone ADA upgrades originally paired with the roof project were deferred at Special Town Meeting so they could be evaluated as part of a larger Neary renovation study.

positions.detail: Supported the project throughout construction and reported in October 2026 that the project is nearly complete with substantial cost savings.
Unanimously supported the revised $4.5 million borrowing authorization at Special Town Meeting after removing standalone ADA upgrades.
Unanimously supported the reduced $4.5 million borrowing request at Special Town Meeting.
Residents strongly supported replacing the failing roof while asking about ballot exclusion risks and ADA triggers, and later urged assessing town-wide deferred maintenance holistically.

northborough-road-chapter-61a-parcel.name: Northborough Road Chapter 61A land acquisition
northborough-road-chapter-61a-parcel.description: Evaluation of town right of first refusal to acquire a 1.47-acre parcel on Northborough Road for affordable housing.
northborough-road-chapter-61a-parcel.status: The town's review of whether to exercise its Chapter 61A right of first refusal to purchase the 1.47-acre Northborough Road parcel for $216,000 has remained behind closed doors, with both the Affordable Housing Trust and Select Board last meeting on the matter in executive session in June 2026. The Affordable Housing Trust has evaluated the site for potential small-scale affordable housing, while the Conservation Commission declined to recommend acquiring the land because of its limited conservation value. The statutory 120-day decision window has elapsed, and no public votes or formal outcomes have been announced.

positions.detail: Evaluated the site's suitability for a duplex or small project and held executive sessions through June 2026 to discuss acquisition negotiations.
Opted on April 2 not to recommend exercising the right of first refusal, citing the parcel's small size and low conservation value.
A resident urged the trust in April to move expeditiously to acquire the parcel for affordable housing and involve the Select Board.

opeb-funding-strategy.name: OPEB liability funding strategy
opeb-funding-strategy.description: Actuarial valuation, liability modeling, and long-term trust contribution strategy for the town's Other Post-Employment Benefits.
opeb-funding-strategy.status: Southborough and the regional school district are reviewing long-term funding strategies to address tens of millions of dollars in unfunded retiree healthcare liabilities. The town's OPEB liability grew to $54.4 million with roughly 8 percent funded in its trust, prompting the Select Board to commission actuarial models for future contribution targets and potential reallocations after county pension obligations finish around 2036. Meanwhile, the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee is weighing a 10-year plan to raise its own annual trust contributions toward an unfunded liability exceeding $48 million.

positions.detail: Agreed on April 28 to have actuaries model several funding scenarios, including redirecting annual pension catch-up payments to OPEB around 2036.
Discussed establishing a 10-year plan to incrementally increase annual trust contributions from the current $25,000.

parkerville-road-utility-pole.name: Parkerville Road utility pole petition
parkerville-road-utility-pole.description: Petition by National Grid and Verizon to install an additional utility pole between poles 101 and 102 on Parkerville Road.
parkerville-road-utility-pole.status: The utility pole petition has been fully approved by the town. The Select Board approved the petition in June after National Grid and town officials agreed to relocate the pole roughly 1,000 feet toward local schools to resolve an abutter's concerns. The Conservation Commission subsequently closed its hearing and issued an Order of Conditions on June 25, 2026, leaving no further town board actions pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 16 to approve the petition after the proposed pole was relocated away from direct abutters.
Voted 5-0 on June 25 to approve an Order of Conditions after receiving a state DEP file number with no substantive objections.

peninsula-trail-phase-1.name: Peninsula Trail Phase 1 closeout
peninsula-trail-phase-1.description: Closeout and accounting of CPA-funded trailheads, parking, and interpretive signs for Peninsula Trail Phase 1, including transferring unspent funds.
peninsula-trail-phase-1.status: Work on Peninsula Trail Phase 1 is complete, including new trailhead kiosks, interpretive signs, and paved parking. The Trails Committee is working to formally close out the Community Preservation Act project after town counsel advised that the project must be closed before Town Meeting can reallocate an unspent $47,000 balance to Phase 2. The next step is presenting closeout documentation to the Community Preservation Committee.

positions.detail: Supports formally closing out Phase 1 so $47,000 in unspent CPA funds can be repurposed for Phase 2 at a future Town Meeting.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.name: Peninsula Trail Phase 2
peninsula-trail-phase-2.description: Scope, wetland crossing design, and construction funding for Phase 2 of the Peninsula Trail.
peninsula-trail-phase-2.status: Town Meeting approved Article 4, authorizing $217,318 in additional Community Preservation Act funds and repurposing $211,232 in prior funding to construct a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge along Route 30. The project passed despite opposition from the Select Board and Advisory Committee, who criticized the $428,550 total budget and high contingency allowances amid municipal operating budget pressures. Backed by the Trails Committee, Community Preservation Committee, Recreation Commission, and Conservation Commission, the bridge is framed as an essential safety connection between regional trail networks. To offset CPA spending, the Trails Committee plans to apply for state grant funding before construction moves toward a December 2029 completion deadline.

positions.detail: Sponsored Article 4 to resolve a pedestrian safety hazard on Route 30, with plans to pursue grant reimbursements to lower net town costs.
Voted 3-2 on Oct 8 to advance Article 4 as printed, maintaining contingency controls and a requirement to seek matching grant funds.
Voted 1-4 on Sep 24 against supporting the article, questioning the roughly $5,000-per-foot bridge cost amid town operating budget strains.
Voted 0-7 on Sep 16 to recommend against approval, citing sticker shock over the $428,550 total cost and questioning contingency sizing.
Voted 5-0 on Jun 25 to send a letter of support for the revised footbridge-only CPA application under its active permit.
Voted 3-0 on Jun 30 to submit a letter of support for the revised CPA application connecting local and regional trails.

peninsula-trail-phase-2.next: MassTrails grant application deadline on February 1, 2027.

personal-property-tax-exemption.name: Personal property tax exemption threshold
personal-property-tax-exemption.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to raise Southborough's personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500.
personal-property-tax-exemption.status: The Board of Assessors' proposal to increase the personal property tax exemption threshold from $1,500 to $2,500 beginning in fiscal year 2028 has unanimous support across town boards. After passing by majority vote at the April 2026 Special Town Meeting, Article 8 was recommended for approval by both the Select Board (5-0) and the Advisory Committee (7-0) in September 2026. The change is designed to eliminate administrative overhead for approximately 22 small business accounts where assessment and collection costs exceed the estimated $200 to $600 in tax revenue generated. No further meetings or votes are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Proposed raising the exemption threshold to $2,500 starting in FY28 to eliminate administrative costs that exceed the tax revenue collected on small accounts.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 15, 2026, to recommend approval of the Special Town Meeting article.
Voted 7-0 on Sep 16, 2026, to recommend approval, citing reduced administrative overhead with minimal tax revenue loss.

plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.name: Plastic bag ban citizen petition
plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.description: Citizen petition bylaw proposal to ban single-use plastic bags in Southborough commercial establishments.
plastic-bag-ban-bylaw.status: The proposed citizen petition to ban single-use plastic checkout bags was withdrawn from the Annual Town Meeting warrant by its student sponsors, who planned to refine the language for fall Town Meeting. The Advisory Committee voted against recommending the original draft, finding it was written as an advisory measure that lacked actionable bylaw language, penalties, and enforcement mechanisms. No updated petition has yet been brought before town boards.

positions.detail: Voted 0-7 on April 6 to recommend disapproval of Article 34, citing the petition's lack of formal bylaw language, penalties, and an enforcement structure.

police-drone-program.name: Police Department drone program
police-drone-program.description: Proposed acquisition of a five-year police drone program package funded through unspent municipal personnel funds.
police-drone-program.status: The Select Board voted 3-2 in June to approve purchasing the five-year, $105,000 police drone package using unspent department personnel surplus, bypassing a Town Meeting appropriation. In August, the Municipal Technology Committee unanimously recommended moving forward under a phased rollout with operational safeguards and reviews scheduled after 90 days and 12 months. With outside funding from Fay School and a state grant offsetting town costs, the department is advancing into a limited initial pilot program.

positions.detail: Voted 3-2 on June 29 to authorize bottom-line surplus spending for the package, reversing its June 16 exclusion over concerns about bypassing Town Meeting.
Voted 3-0 on June 24 to endorse the drone program as an immediate capital safety priority, deferring the funding mechanism to the Select Board.
Voted 4-0 on August 27 to recommend conditional approval and phased deployment with privacy limits and 90-day and 12-month formal reviews.

preschool-tuition-and-assistance.name: Public preschool tuition and financial assistance
preschool-tuition-and-assistance.description: Setting annual tuition rates and income-based financial assistance policies for Southborough public preschool programs.
preschool-tuition-and-assistance.status: The School Committee unanimously approved a 3% preschool tuition increase and updated financial assistance guidelines for the district's program. The new financial assistance policy caps total aid at 10% of annual program tuition revenue, providing tiered reductions of up to 90% based on federal poverty levels. With rates having remained flat since FY22, the adjustments were implemented to cover rising operational and labor expenses.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 8, 2026, to approve the 3% tuition increase and the revised financial assistance guidelines.

presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.name: Presidential and Fisher Road waterline looping
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.description: MWRA loan funding and construction to connect dead-end water mains under CSX railroad tracks along Presidential Drive and Fisher Road.
presidential-fisher-waterline-looping.status: The $1 million waterline looping project between Presidential Drive and Fisher Road is approved and funded. Following Town Meeting's authorization of $1 million in borrowing in April 2026, the Select Board voted unanimously in August 2026 to submit the zero-interest loan application to the Massachusetts Water Resources Authority. The project will connect two dead-end water mains under the CSX railroad tracks to improve water quality and pressure, with debt service repaid over roughly ten years through water rates.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Aug 11, 2026, to authorize the town's $1 million MWRA zero-interest loan application.
Approved Article 11 by a two-thirds majority on Apr 11, 2026, authorizing $1,000,000 in borrowing for the project.
Deferred making a recommendation in March 2026 to evaluate water rate impacts and Select Board deliberations at Town Meeting.

recreation-capital-plan.name: Recreation multi-year capital plan
recreation-capital-plan.description: Five-year capital requests, facility master planning, and field improvement scheduling by the Recreation Commission.
recreation-capital-plan.status: The Recreation Commission's multi-year capital plan is currently under review by the Capital Improvement and Planning Committee after the commission deferred a $50,000 athletic facility master plan to FY29 to align with the Neary School building study. The capital committee is seeking to clarify whether the commission's FY28 park maintenance request is $25,000 or $50,000 due to conflicting spreadsheet figures. The committee chair plans to verify that line item amount and track a separate funding application for a dog park before the Community Preservation Committee.

positions.detail: Voted 3-0 on Sep 17 to approve its updated capital plan, deferring a facility master plan to FY29 and requesting $25,000 for FY28 park maintenance.
Reviewing the submission while seeking confirmation on whether the FY28 maintenance request is $25,000 or $50,000.

regional-fire-department-study.name: Regional fire and EMS feasibility study
regional-fire-department-study.description: Feasibility study and intermunicipal discussions with Westborough regarding potential regionalization of fire and emergency medical services.
regional-fire-department-study.status: Southborough and Westborough officials held preliminary discussions in early 2026 to explore a joint feasibility study on regionalizing fire and emergency medical services. The Select Board received an informational update in March 2026 but did not take a formal stance or vote on the initiative. No further public discussions or formal proposals have been scheduled.

regional-school-athletic-complex-bond.name: Regional School athletic complex bond sale
regional-school-athletic-complex-bond.description: Issuance and sale of general obligation bonds to fund the Algonquin Regional High School athletic complex and amenities building.
regional-school-athletic-complex-bond.status: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee unanimously approved the issuance and sale of $7.115 million in general obligation bonds to finance the Algonquin Regional High School athletic complex and amenities building. Competitive bidding allowed the district to resize the bond issue downward from $7.735 million while securing a 3.07 percent true interest rate with Loop Capital Markets LLC. The financing is finalized, with total debt service running through June 2039.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on June 17, 2026, to approve the sale of $7.115 million in bonds to Loop Capital Markets LLC.

regional-school-calendar-2026-2027.name: 2026-2027 regional school calendar
regional-school-calendar-2026-2027.description: School year schedule planning, religious holiday observances, and professional development day placement for the 2026-2027 academic year.
regional-school-calendar-2026-2027.status: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee approved calendar Option 5 for the 2026-2027 academic year in a 4-1-1 vote, aligning with Southborough's earlier approval. The adopted schedule places the first day of school on September 1, 2026, removes professional development days from Yom Kippur and Eid, and designates a professional development day on Orthodox Good Friday. No further action or review is pending before the regional committee.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1-1 on Feb 25 to adopt Option 5, reconsidering its December 2025 vote to align regional high school operations with member towns.
Residents split between supporting regional alignment and arguing that school calendars should recognize only federal holidays to ensure equal treatment across faith backgrounds.

regional-school-calendar-2027-2028.name: 2027-2028 regional school calendar
regional-school-calendar-2027-2028.description: Planning, religious holiday observance, and vacation structure for the 2027-2028 regional school year calendar.
regional-school-calendar-2027-2028.status: The regional and local school committees are reviewing the framework for the 2027–2028 academic calendar, focusing on religious holiday observances and the final day of classes. Members are evaluating whether to maintain the current holiday schedule, remove certain religious holidays, or adjust vacations and start dates so winter snow days do not push the school year late into June. The administration plans to gather staff and family feedback this fall before presenting formal options on December 2, 2026.

positions.detail: Discussing multiple calendar structures on September 16, balancing religious holiday observances against concerns about snow days extending the school year past June 25.
A resident urged the committees to continue including major Jewish holidays on the calendar and to maintain current religious holiday observances.

regional-school-calendar-2027-2028.next: Administration presents calendar options and survey feedback on December 2, 2026.

regional-school-religious-observance-pol.name: Regional school religious observance policy
regional-school-religious-observance-pol.description: Review, communication, and enforcement of School Committee Policy I-340 governing student accommodations on religious and cultural holidays.
regional-school-religious-observance-pol.status: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee is addressing the enforcement of Policy I-340, which requires academic accommodations without penalty for students observing religious and cultural holidays. The review follows parent feedback citing inconsistent compliance by teaching staff during recent holidays. The committee referred the matter to its policy subcommittee and the administration to establish advance calendar reminders and annual staff communication.

positions.detail: Supports strengthening districtwide communication and teacher adherence to ensure students are accommodated during religious observances.

regional-superintendent-evaluation-and-c.name: Superintendent evaluation and contract
regional-superintendent-evaluation-and-c.description: Evaluation goals, annual performance reviews, and contract salary adjustments for the regional superintendent of schools.
regional-superintendent-evaluation-and-c.status: All four school committees approved a $22,750 market adjustment to Superintendent Gregory Martineau's contract on September 16, 2026, increasing his 2026–2027 base salary to $270,213 retroactive to July 1. The committees also approved his 2026–2027 evaluation goals, which focus on leadership transitions and major capital projects, including Southborough's Neary School project. Officials confirmed the salary increase will be absorbed within current operating budgets without requiring additional tax revenue. A mid-cycle evaluation update is scheduled for December 2, 2026.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 to approve the salary market adjustment and 4-0 to approve the 2026–2027 evaluation goals on September 16.
Voted unanimously on September 16 to approve both the salary adjustment and the 2026–2027 evaluation goals.
Voted 4-1 on September 16 to approve the salary adjustment and unanimously to approve the evaluation goals.
Voted 6-0 to approve the salary adjustment and 5-0 to approve the evaluation goals on September 16.

regional-superintendent-evaluation-and-c.next: Superintendent mid-cycle evaluation update at the combined School Committee meeting on December 2, 2026.

rescinding-unissued-borrowing.name: Rescission of unissued borrowing authorizations
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting warrant article to rescind unused borrowing authorizations for completed capital projects, including Breakneck Hill and the Neary School study.
rescinding-unissued-borrowing.status: A Special Town Meeting warrant article proposes rescinding $1,102,960 in unused borrowing authorizations from the completed Breakneck Hill Farm dump remediation ($727,960) and Neary School feasibility study ($375,000). The Select Board and Advisory Committee support the full rescission to clear the town's debt books, unanimously rejecting a request from the Conservation Commission and Stewardship Committee to hold back $100,000 for site restoration. Although Special Town Meeting voted to approve rescinding these authorizations in April 2026, the rescission was placed back on the warrant for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, whose outcome is not yet recorded.

positions.detail: Voted to recommend Article 6 and unanimously opposed offering a floor amendment to retain $100,000, noting $176,000 in cash remains available.
Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend Article 6 to clear unneeded debt authorizations from town records.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 17 to request reducing the rescission by $100,000 to retain borrowing capacity for Breakneck Hill restoration, a request the Select Board rejected.
Requested retaining $100,000 in borrowing authorization for habitat restoration and road repairs, which the Select Board declined to support.
Voted by majority on Apr 11 to approve rescinding $1,102,960 in borrowing authority across the Breakneck Hill and Neary School accounts.

reserve-fund-transfer-policy.name: Reserve Fund transfer policy
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.description: Advisory Committee policy setting standard procedures, executive board oversight, and statutory criteria for departmental Reserve Fund transfer requests.
reserve-fund-transfer-policy.status: The Advisory Committee is updating its Reserve Fund transfer policy to tighten oversight and ensure statutory compliance for departmental funding requests. Proposed revisions require vetting by the Town Administrator, notification to the Capital Improvement Planning Committee for capital items, and prior approval from departmental executive boards, while strictly barring reimbursements for already incurred expenses. The committee has prepared a clean working draft and is expected to take a final vote on the policy at a future meeting.

positions.detail: Drafting stricter rules to require administrative vetting and executive board sign-off while barring retroactive reimbursements.

route-9-495-gateway-study.name: Route 9 and I-495 gateway corridor study
route-9-495-gateway-study.description: A joint $150,000 planning and infrastructure study with Westborough evaluating economic development, zoning, and infrastructure along the Route 9 and I-495 corridor.
route-9-495-gateway-study.status: Southborough and Westborough are awaiting an announcement from the state on a joint $150,000 Community One Stop for Growth grant application to fund an infrastructure, zoning, and regional wastewater study along the Route 9 and Interstate 495 corridor. The Select Board, Planning Board, and Wastewater Study Committee all support the initiative, which requires a $7,500 local cash match from each town. The Wastewater Study Committee has paused regular meetings and hiring engineering consultants until grant awards are announced in October 2026.

positions.detail: Supported the joint grant application and paused further meetings and consultant hiring pending state award announcements.
Voted 4-0 on May 21, 2026, to endorse a letter of support after adding language to protect residential buffers and focus on commercial tax base growth.
Voted 5-0 on May 19, 2026, to approve a letter of support for the joint grant application.

route-9-495-gateway-study.next: State grant award announcements expected in October 2026.

route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.name: Route 9 wastewater infrastructure plan
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.description: Planning, site evaluation, and District Improvement Financing for wastewater collection and treatment along the Route 9 corridor.
route-9-wastewater-infrastructure.status: Planning for an estimated $40 million to $50 million municipal wastewater system along Route 9 is under review, with the Wastewater Study Committee targeting the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The committee opted not to bring articles to the fall 2026 Special Town Meeting, concluding it needed more time to establish cost projections, site selection, and state environmental permitting for watershed zones and potential interbasin water transfers. While the Select Board voted 4-1 in June to authorize $30,000 for economic modeling to support a District Improvement Financing (DIF) district, the study committee voted 0-5 against funding that specific consultant study later that month.

positions.detail: Targeting the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting for a modular Route 9 treatment and collection proposal, deferring action from the fall to resolve site, engineering, and MassDEP regulatory issues.
Voted 4-1 in June to allocate $30,000 from Economic Development Committee funds for financial analysis of a Route 9 financing district, and extended the study committee's charge through June 2027.

ruby-estates-subdivision.name: Ruby Estates subdivision
ruby-estates-subdivision.description: Six-lot residential subdivision along Lampson Drive off Mount Vickery Road.
ruby-estates-subdivision.status: The Planning Board approved a surety agreement and voted unanimously in June 2026 to release all six lots of the Ruby Estates subdivision from the municipal covenant. The release followed developer Bartolini Builders' installation of utilities and roadway binder course for Lampson Drive, secured by an approved construction completion bond of $324,140.81. No further board reviews or actions are currently pending.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to accept the surety agreement and release all six lots from the subdivision covenant.

rural-cemetery-water-tower.name: Rural Cemetery stone water tower restoration
rural-cemetery-water-tower.description: Proposed structural evaluation, restoration, and Community Preservation Act funding for the historic stone water tower in Rural Cemetery.
rural-cemetery-water-tower.status: The proposed Community Preservation Act funding application to restore the historic Rural Cemetery stone water tower has been deferred to the spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting round. The delay allows the project consultant time to complete necessary architectural documentation, bid specifications, and a maintenance schedule. A previous concept to adapt the tower interior into a columbarium has been dropped after the Cemetery Committee showed no interest.

positions.detail: Is advancing a CPA application for a structural restoration study, historic documentation, and bid specifications for the tower.
Agreed on Aug 3 to defer review of the application to the spring funding round to accommodate consultant preparation time.
Confirmed it has no interest in repurposing the interior of the water tower as a columbarium.

salary-administration-plan-amendments.name: Salary Administration Plan amendments
salary-administration-plan-amendments.description: Proposed warrant articles to amend the non-union Salary Administration Plan bylaw, salary grids, and stipend schedules.
salary-administration-plan-amendments.status: The Salary Administration Plan amendments were adopted by Town Meeting on April 11, 2026, under Article 4. The measure updated compensation schedules for non-union personnel, incorporating a 3% cost-of-living adjustment, modified acting department head pay, and new stipends. With Town Meeting approval completed, the revised personnel bylaw is now in effect and no further action is pending.

positions.detail: Voted on April 11, 2026, to pass Article 4 updating the town's non-union personnel bylaw and compensation schedules.
Voted 4-0 on March 10, 2026, to approve the final bylaw amendments and summary for the Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 5-0 on March 10, 2026, to recommend approval of Article 4 as part of a grouped warrant vote.
A municipal employee expressed concern in March 2026 that non-union staff faced low morale and vulnerability amid Select Board discussions about cutting positions.

sarsenstone-way-coc.name: Sarsenstone Way Certificate of Compliance
sarsenstone-way-coc.description: Certificate of Compliance review and archival records search for the 1970s Sarsenstone Way subdivision under DEP file 290-100.
sarsenstone-way-coc.status: The Conservation Commission approved a full Certificate of Compliance for the Sarsenstone Way subdivision on August 27, 2026, closing out DEP File 290-100. The commission had previously issued a partial certificate in July for two vacant parcels undergoing probate while staff searched town archives for missing documentation. The full release was granted after the conservation agent located historic Department of Public Works as-built plans confirming drainage and roadway requirements were satisfied.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on August 27 to approve a full Certificate of Compliance after historic DPW plans verified that subdivision conditions were met.

scenic-road-tree-removals.name: DPW scenic road tree removals
scenic-road-tree-removals.description: Tree Warden and DPW hearings and approvals to trim or remove public shade trees along designated scenic roads.
scenic-road-tree-removals.status: The Planning Board unanimously approved the DPW's application to remove four hazardous trees and trim another along designated scenic roads following an April 2026 joint hearing with the Tree Warden. The vote followed earlier procedural concerns raised by board members over trees being removed under state 'imminent hazard' exemptions without public notice or hearings. Town officials also discussed developing a GIS inventory to track trees and pursuing replacement plantings owed by utility companies. No further hearings or steps are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 27, 2026, to approve the four scenic road tree removals and one trimming due to decay, cavities, and safety hazards.
Speakers inquired about prioritizing hazard removals on streets reliant on private well power and asked about the status of replacement plantings owed by utility companies.

school-bus-transportation-operations.name: School bus transportation and technology
school-bus-transportation-operations.description: Bus operations, safety tracking technologies, and vendor performance oversight with contractor NRT.
school-bus-transportation-operations.status: School bus operations under contractor NRT have stabilized, with live security cameras and turn-by-turn GPS active, though student RFID tap cards have faced rollout delays. The school district administration moved to assess contract penalties against NRT to withhold payment for delayed technology deliverables. The Southborough School Committee received the operational update without taking a formal vote, and no further public reviews are currently scheduled.

school-choice-participation.name: Interdistrict school choice participation
school-choice-participation.description: Annual School Committee evaluation and hearing on whether to participate in the Massachusetts interdistrict school choice program.
school-choice-participation.status: Both the Southborough School Committee and the Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee voted unanimously in April 2026 to opt out of the state interdistrict school choice program for the 2026-2027 school year. Both committees cited target class size limits and the gap between the $5,000 state reimbursement and local per-pupil operating costs exceeding $23,000. Enrollment remains restricted to local residents for the academic year, with the decision reviewed annually.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on April 8, 2026, to opt out of school choice, citing class size limits and a per-pupil operating cost of $23,911 versus the $5,000 state reimbursement.
Voted unanimously on April 15, 2026, to opt out for the 2026-2027 year, citing Algonquin's $25,042 per-pupil cost compared to the $5,000 state tuition rate and class size constraints.

school-district-capital-borrowing-fy27.name: FY27 school district capital borrowing
school-district-capital-borrowing-fy27.description: Borrowing authorization for district-wide school capital projects including technology upgrades, security systems, and Finn School flooring.
school-district-capital-borrowing-fy27.status: Town Meeting approved a $2,575,000 capital borrowing authorization for district schools under Article 12 in April 2026. The funding covers $365,000 for classroom technology upgrades, $1,400,000 for district-wide security and emergency communication systems, and $810,000 for flooring replacement and moisture mitigation at Finn School. A floor motion seeking to strip out the $1.4 million security component failed before the main borrowing authorization passed by a two-thirds majority.

positions.detail: Approved the $2,575,000 borrowing authorization by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, after defeating an amendment to remove security funding.
Speakers divided over the $1.4 million security borrowing, with opponents questioning debt for details not discussed in open session and supporters citing first responder coordination.

school-district-opioid-settlement-alloca.name: Regional school district opioid settlement allocation
school-district-opioid-settlement-alloca.description: Request to allocate a portion of Southborough and Northborough municipal opioid settlement funds to the regional school district.
school-district-opioid-settlement-alloca.status: A request to allocate a portion of Southborough's municipal opioid settlement funds to the regional school district remains pending before the Board of Health. In April 2026, the board deferred action until after both Southborough and Northborough concluded their spring town meetings. A formal proposal to fund shared substance use prevention programming has not yet come up for a vote.

positions.detail: Tabled discussion in April pending spring town meetings and has not yet voted on the funding allocation.

school-food-service-contract.name: School food service contract renewal
school-food-service-contract.description: Contract administration, financial performance, and annual renewals for district food services with Whitsons Culinary Group.
school-food-service-contract.status: Contracts with Whitsons Culinary Group were extended for the 2026–2027 school year after both school committees approved one-year renewals in May, despite an initial failed vote and reconsideration at the regional level over meal quality and staffing. Whitsons has since introduced a new district general manager, added dedicated kitchen management, and revised menu options in response to student surveys and staff feedback. Administration will conduct a quarterly review in December to evaluate financial performance and decide whether to rebid or continue the contract into a third year.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on May 13 to extend the contract for 2026–2027, and received favorable reports in October on new kitchen management and expanded menu initiatives.
Now supports; voted 8-1 on reconsideration on May 20 to approve the contract extension after an initial 3-4-2 vote failed over concerns about food quality and staff morale.
A high school cafeteria employee cited low staff morale, meal shortages, and dissatisfaction with frozen processed items replacing homemade food.

school-food-service-contract.next: Quarterly financial and participation review in December 2026

senior-tax-work-off-policy.name: Senior Tax Work-Off policy and slot allocation
senior-tax-work-off-policy.description: Eligibility regulations and position allocations for Southborough's Senior Tax Work-Off property tax abatement program.
senior-tax-work-off-policy.status: The Senior Tax Work-Off Policy is approved and in effect following Select Board action. The board expanded the program from 30 to 40 participant positions in April 2026 and updated eligibility rules. In September 2026, the board unanimously re-approved the policy with amendments requiring CORI background checks and clarifying exclusions from other municipal employee benefits.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on September 2 to re-approve the policy with CORI requirements and benefit exclusions after expanding the program to 40 slots in April.

southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.name: Southborough Golf Club Audubon management plan
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.description: Consultant RFP and environmental management plan to achieve Audubon International certification for the Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-audubon-plan.status: The Southborough Golf Club's Audubon International certification effort is moving toward a consultant contract after the Golf Committee voted on October 13, 2026, to commit up to $4,500 from its revolving fund to cover a budget deficit. Conservation Works submitted the sole proposal of $18,400, which exceeded the remaining balance of the project's 2018 Community Preservation Act appropriation. Town procurement staff are now working to finalize the contract while the committee looks to negotiate lower costs with the consultant.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on October 13 to cover the consultant's $4,500 funding shortfall from the revolving fund and to pay past-due Audubon membership dues.
Residents have questioned the eight-year span since the initial 2018 appropriation without project completion and asked about historical costs and efforts.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.name: Southborough Golf Club irrigation replacement
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.description: Planning, value engineering, and Community Preservation Act funding for replacing the irrigation system at Southborough Golf Club.
southborough-golf-club-irrigation.status: Special Town Meeting approved Article 3 by majority vote, appropriating $433,546 in Community Preservation Act funds paired with $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund for a $1.09 million irrigation overhaul. The project had the unanimous backing of the Select Board and recommendation from the Community Preservation Committee, but faced unanimous opposition from the Advisory Committee, which argued the self-sustaining course should fund capital work through golfer surcharges. Prior to the vote, the Golf Committee mounted an extensive voter outreach campaign and opted not to seek floor amendments to decouple the new funding from an extension of $550,000 in expiring 2024 authorizations.

positions.detail: Approved Article 3 by majority vote to allocate $433,546 in CPA funds toward the irrigation project.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 24 to support revised Article 3 on the Special Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 4-1 on Sep 14 to recommend the warrant article with environmental and revolving-fund conditions.
Sponsored the project and voted unanimously on Oct 6 to spend up to $500 on voter outreach flyers.
Reached consensus on Aug 27 supporting the directional boring design and pump station placement under the conservation restriction.
Voted 0-7 on Sep 16 against recommending Article 3, maintaining the golf course should fund capital needs through user fees.
Comments ranged from support for maintaining the course as a vital community space to opposition over using town preservation funds instead of user fees.

southborough-golf-club-irrigation.next: Select Board procurement process for golf course management contract by April 1, 2027.

sta-unit-a-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit A contract
sta-unit-a-contract.description: Collective bargaining agreement and amendments between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit A teachers.
sta-unit-a-contract.status: The Southborough School Committee voted unanimously on October 14, 2026, to approve contract amendments to the collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The changes revise the retirement incentive program and align Southborough's teacher salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School effective July 1, 2027. No further board action is currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on Oct 14 to approve amendments revising retirement incentives and aligning the teacher salary schedule to Algonquin.

sta-unit-c-contract.name: Southborough Teachers Association Unit C contract
sta-unit-c-contract.description: Three-year collective bargaining agreement between the Southborough School Committee and the Southborough Teachers Association covering Unit C support staff.
sta-unit-c-contract.status: The Southborough School Committee unanimously approved a three-year collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association for Unit C on June 18, 2026. The contract covers administrative assistants and educational support professionals across the district. The finalized agreement was set to become public following ratification by both parties.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 18, 2026, to approve the three-year contract, citing collaborative and productive negotiations.

stewardship-committee-structure.name: Stewardship Committee structure and merger proposal
stewardship-committee-structure.description: Deliberation over committee appointments and a proposal to merge the Stewardship Committee with the Open Space Preservation Commission.
stewardship-committee-structure.status: The Select Board resolved an appointment impasse on August 11, 2026, by voting 4-1 to amend the Stewardship Committee's charge to convert a representative seat into a fourth at-large position and unanimously appointing Freddie Gillespie. That action followed the board's June decision not to reappoint Gillespie to the Open Space Preservation Commission, which had stripped her of her designated Stewardship seat. Both the Stewardship Committee and the Conservation Commission oppose merging Stewardship with Open Space, arguing the committee must remain an independent body focused strictly on managing Breakneck Hill and the Town Forest. While the immediate appointment is settled, broader reviews of conservation and open space committee consolidation remain open for future discussion.

positions.detail: Amended the Stewardship charge 4-1 on August 11 to create an at-large seat and appointed Freddie Gillespie 5-0, while keeping broader committee consolidation open for future review.
Opposes merging with the Open Space Preservation Commission, arguing it should remain an independent ad-hoc body dedicated strictly to land management.
Voted 5-0 on June 25 to send a letter opposing consolidation of the two committees and supporting Freddie Gillespie's reappointment.
Commenters praised Freddie Gillespie's decades of conservation achievements and urged the Select Board to retain experienced volunteers.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.name: Stormwater enterprise fund
stormwater-enterprise-fund.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article to establish a municipal enterprise fund for stormwater management accounting and future funding.
stormwater-enterprise-fund.status: Town Meeting approved Article 5 establishing a dedicated stormwater enterprise fund effective July 1, 2027, creating an accounting mechanism while leaving fees and operating budgets for future approval. The Select Board and Advisory Committee both support the fund to shift costs away from residential property taxes toward impervious surface area, though concerns remain over taxpayer impact and potential fees. Specific fee structures and the initial operating budget are scheduled for consideration at the Spring 2027 Annual Town Meeting.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on Sep 15 to recommend approval of Article 5 to transition stormwater funding toward an impervious-surface user model.
Voted 7-0 on Sep 16 to recommend approval of Article 5, noting it establishes the accounting framework for FY28 without setting fees.
Approved Article 5 by majority vote on Apr 11 to establish the stormwater enterprise fund effective July 1, 2027.
A resident asked who would pay into the fund and whether parcels with private stormwater systems would receive exemptions.

stormwater-enterprise-fund.next: Annual Town Meeting consideration of fee structure and operating budget in Spring 2027

street-tree-planting-program.name: Street tree planting pilot study
street-tree-planting-program.description: A pilot study and planting program to evaluate street canopy cover and identify replacement tree planting locations.
street-tree-planting-program.status: The Planning Board approved a $5,500 pilot study in June 2026 to evaluate canopy cover along 10 to 15 streets starting from the town center and locate roughly 25 viable replacement tree planting sites. The effort, funded through the tree fund, aims to address canopy loss from utility removals and development projects. A designated Planning Board liaison is coordinating with the tree warden on long-term planning.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on June 22, 2026, to approve the $5,500 pilot study proposal from Davey Resource Group.

subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.name: Subdivision Rules and Regulations review
subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.description: Comprehensive review and modernization of Southborough's subdivision rules, regulations, and ANR procedures by the Planning Board.
subdivision-rules-and-regulations-update.status: The Planning Board's working group continues to draft a comprehensive update to Southborough's subdivision rules, regulations, and ANR procedures. The working group has been testing a restructured document format and plans to consult Town Counsel regarding the opening definitions section. Drafting remains underway, and the revisions have not yet been brought to the full board for formal review.

tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.name: Delinquent tax payment agreement bylaw
tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.description: Proposed Town Meeting warrant article accepting state statute to authorize formal payment agreements for delinquent property taxes.
tax-payment-agreements-bylaw.status: The proposed warrant article to authorize formal installment payment agreements for delinquent property taxes has the unanimous backing of town boards. Both the Select Board and the Advisory Committee voted in March 2026 to support Article 29, which accepts a state statute allowing the town treasurer to set up payment plans and waive up to 50% of accrued interest. The measure is aimed at addressing roughly 30 active tax liens in town.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on March 10, 2026, to support placing Article 29 on the Town Meeting warrant.
Voted 5-0 on March 16, 2026, to recommend approval of Article 29.

town-budget-process-policy.name: Town budget process policy
town-budget-process-policy.description: Draft municipal policy formalizing timelines, board responsibilities, and procedures for constructing the annual town omnibus budget.
town-budget-process-policy.status: The Advisory Committee is revising a draft municipal policy that defines timelines and roles for assembling the annual town budget, seeking to preserve its statutory authority to independently evaluate, recommend, and present the budget at Town Meeting. Members expressed concern that earlier drafts omitted school spending and included language requiring consensus with the Select Board. The committee agreed to finalize its proposed revisions to share with the Select Board, but no further hearings are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Supported formalizing the process but revised the draft to protect its independent role in presenting the final budget at Town Meeting and noted the draft excludes school spending.

town-common-fence-restoration.name: Town Common fence restoration
town-common-fence-restoration.description: Repair and restoration of the historic fence and railings at the Town Common funded by the Community Preservation Act.
town-common-fence-restoration.status: The project is under contract after the Select Board voted in June 2026 to award a $70,500 base restoration bid to Kneeland Construction, with construction required to finish by the end of the year. Procurement rules prevented awarding an add-alternate to replace a section of fence lost during state highway work. The town plans to either pursue funding or replacement from MassDOT or bid that missing section separately at a later date.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on June 2, 2026, to award the base restoration bid to Kneeland Construction.

town-forest-footbridge.name: Town Forest Eagle Scout footbridge
town-forest-footbridge.description: Construction materials, permitting, and approvals for an Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest.
town-forest-footbridge.status: The Stewardship Committee voted 4-0 in August to approve the use of pre-cut, pressure-treated lumber for the Eagle Scout footbridge project in the Town Forest. The decision followed earlier concerns raised through the Trails Committee regarding chemical leaching near a vernal pool and wetland crossing. No further committee hearings or construction dates are currently scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted 4-0 on Aug 4 to authorize the pre-cut treated lumber, citing research that modern pressure-treated wood causes minimal copper leaching.
Agreed on Jun 1 to gather technical specifications and consult regional conservation officials after concerns were raised regarding pressure-treated wood near wetlands.

town-governance-study.name: Town governance structure study
town-governance-study.description: A consultant-led study evaluating Southborough's municipal government structure, town manager authority, and committee organization.
town-governance-study.status: A consultant-led review of Southborough's municipal government structure is underway following an initial briefing to the Select Board in early October. The study is evaluating town administrator authority, committee organization, and potential charter or bylaw updates. A public listening session and individual board member interviews are slated for November, with a final report targeted for December.

positions.detail: Voted 4-1 on Aug 11 to fund the $24,650 study to explore administrative efficiencies, with one member dissenting over spending during tight budget conditions.

town-governance-study.next: Public listening session in early November 2026

town-satisfaction-survey.name: 2026 Town Satisfaction Survey
town-satisfaction-survey.description: Design, public outreach, and execution of the townwide resident satisfaction survey conducted by the Municipal Technology Committee.
town-satisfaction-survey.status: The 2026 Southborough Satisfaction Survey is currently underway, running from October 1 through November 30. The Municipal Technology Committee streamlined and shortened this year's questions to improve completion rates following drop-offs in 2025, while adding new sections on senior services and affordable housing. The Affordable Housing Trust contributed revisions to the housing questions, and the Select Board endorsed a framework to address department service findings.

positions.detail: Redesigned and launched the survey to run through November 30, shortening question matrices to improve completion rates and adding questions on housing and senior services.
Reviewed and submitted refined housing questions for the survey, advising clearer terminology for workforce housing and focusing questions on the downtown area.
Endorsed the committee's 90-day action plan on September 2 to address resident feedback on municipal services from the previous survey.

town-website-redesign.name: Town website redesign
town-website-redesign.description: Redesign of the municipal website with vendor CivicPlus and consolidation of standalone departmental pages.
town-website-redesign.status: The town is preparing for a scheduled triennial website redesign and refresh with vendor CivicPlus, planned to kick off in October 2026. The Municipal Technology Committee is working to consolidate standalone departmental pages into the main platform, including migrating Senior Center content and assessing recreation software. Committee members have noted that the project will require dedicated communications guidance alongside technical staff to ensure consistent messaging across departments.

positions.detail: Supports the triennial redesign and site consolidation with CivicPlus, while emphasizing the need for professional communications expertise to manage outward content.

town-website-redesign.next: Town IT staff kickoff meeting with CivicPlus in October 2026.

transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.name: Transfer station fees and regulations
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.description: Department of Public Works updates to transfer station sticker pricing, outside hauling costs, and operational rules for disposal.
transfer-station-fees-and-regulations.status: The Select Board approved fiscal year 2027 transfer station permit fees in July and adopted updated operational regulations on August 11, which clarified Swap Shop guidelines and excluded child car seats on health guidance. On September 2, the board voted unanimously to continue participating in a 35-town municipal consortium negotiating bulk disposal rates ahead of the town's contract expiration in December 2027. The Department of Public Works plans to install simplified signage at the facility to inform residents of the updated rules.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously to adopt the revised regulations in August and to remain in the regional waste consortium in September, after voting 5-0 in July to set FY27 sticker fees.

tricentennial-firefighters-muster.name: 2027 Tricentennial Firefighter's Muster
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.description: Organization of a regional firefighter's muster and antique hand tub demonstration at Woodward School in July 2027.
tricentennial-firefighters-muster.status: Planning for the 2027 Tricentennial antique firefighter's muster is underway with an approved budget of $25,000. Eight regional hand tub teams have confirmed participation out of an expected 16 to 20, and catering and live entertainment have been booked. Organizers are currently restoring Southborough's two historic hand tubs and are preparing site and parking layouts for review.

positions.detail: Voted 6-0 on June 10, 2026, to approve a budget up to $25,000 and is actively reviewing event logistics.

tricentennial-first-day.name: First Day 2027 celebration
tricentennial-first-day.description: Planning for Southborough's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration featuring family activities, a drone show, and a bonfire.
tricentennial-first-day.status: Planning is underway for the town's January 1, 2027 Tricentennial kickoff celebration following execution of a contract with Firefly for a 200-drone light show launching from St. Mark's School. Logistics for other activities remain in flux, as the committee is reconsidering horse-drawn hayrides due to quotes exceeding $5,000 and evaluating alternative sites or dates for a community bonfire because of turf and wiring concerns at Woodward School. Middle school student art submissions for custom drone formations are due November 17, with the committee expected to finalize event details at its November meeting.

positions.detail: Contracted the drone show vendor and is adjusting site logistics, including wagon rides and bonfire locations, ahead of the celebration.

tricentennial-first-day.next: Trottier Middle School student artwork submissions due November 17, 2026

tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.name: GloSoBo Tricentennial light festival
tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.description: Planning, funding, and programming for the GloSoBo winter light celebration scheduled as part of the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-glosobo-winter-lights.status: The Tricentennial Committee has formally approved adding the GloSoBo winter light celebration to the official 2027 Tricentennial calendar. The evening event is tentatively scheduled for December 3, 2027, in the town center with an estimated budget ceiling of $10,000. Further planning and logistics remain to be developed as the celebration approaches.

positions.detail: Voted 5-0 on April 8, 2026, to include GloSoBo in the official Tricentennial calendar.

tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.name: 2027 Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.description: Planning for an expanded Heritage Day Parade in October 2027 featuring marching units, community floats, and a historic cannon.
tricentennial-heritage-day-parade.status: Planning is underway for an expanded Tricentennial Heritage Day Parade in October 2027. The Tricentennial Committee is evaluating adjustments including a Sunday 1:00 PM kickoff, alternate staging and de-staging areas, and historic artillery demonstrations. Organizers are preparing to coordinate proposed routes and staging plans with the police and fire departments.

positions.detail: Supports expanding the 2027 parade and is coordinating route, timing, and safety logistics with public safety officials.

tricentennial-house-tour.name: 2027 Tricentennial historic house tour
