tricentennial-house-tour.description: Planning and volunteer coordination for a historic house tour celebration for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-house-tour.status: Planning is underway for the Tricentennial historic house tour scheduled for September 18, 2027. Eleven properties are currently committed toward a goal of 10 to 12 stops, with addresses kept confidential until closer to the date. Next steps include recruiting at least 20 volunteer docents, pursuing local business partnerships, and finalizing a proposed $5,000 budget for materials and public safety details.

positions.detail: Advancing event logistics, docent recruitment, and a proposed $5,000 budget for the September 18, 2027 tour.

tricentennial-street-banners.name: Tricentennial commemorative street banners
tricentennial-street-banners.description: Permitting and installation of celebratory banners on utility poles across Southborough's historic villages.
tricentennial-street-banners.status: Following Town Meeting's approval of a temporary sign bylaw amendment in April 2026, town staff and the Tricentennial Committee are coordinating attachment permits with National Grid and Verizon. The committee recently directed staff to finalize a list capped at 50 poles, reduced from an initial 87, in order to avoid utility inspection fees. Staff are currently preparing required insurance and administrative filings so the celebratory banners can be installed across town.

positions.detail: Promoting the banner initiative and directed staff in October 2026 to cap pole selections at 50 to avoid utility inspection fees.
Approved Article 32 by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, temporarily amending the sign bylaw to allow celebratory banners through January 31, 2028.
Reviewed the 50-banner proposal in June 2026 and directed town administration to coordinate pole permits with utility companies.
Supported Article 32 ahead of Town Meeting to authorize the temporary banner zoning amendment.

tricentennial-summer-nights.name: Summer Nights 2027 music festival
tricentennial-summer-nights.description: Expansion of the annual Summer Nights community event into a multi-act music festival for the 2027 Tricentennial.
tricentennial-summer-nights.status: Planning is underway to expand the annual Summer Nights event into a full-day music festival at the Neary School grounds on August 21, 2027, to celebrate Southborough's Tricentennial. Organizers are finalizing headliner contracts and examining property parcel boundaries to determine whether a beer garden could be permitted under school alcohol policies. Working group organizers will next coordinate staging, permitting, and site layout with police, fire, recreation, and town administration.

positions.detail: Supports expanding the 2027 event with multiple musical acts, food trucks, and fireworks, and is coordinating logistics and grant funding.

tricentennial-time-capsule.name: Tricentennial time capsule
tricentennial-time-capsule.description: Selection, preservation, and public placement of a commemorative time capsule for Southborough's 300th anniversary.
tricentennial-time-capsule.status: The Tricentennial Committee is moving forward with plans for a 2-foot cube commemorative time capsule designated for indoor storage at the Harvard Depository to avoid water damage. Working groups are preparing formal invitations to local civic organizations, clubs, and schools to submit historical artifacts and archival-grade photo prints. Boy Scout Troop 1 has volunteered to help coordinate item collection.

positions.detail: Supports an archival-grade capsule stored indoors at the Harvard Depository and is preparing to solicit submissions from local organizations.

trottier-finn-expansion-studies.name: Trottier and Finn expansion feasibility studies
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.description: Proposed Special Town Meeting articles to study expanding Trottier and Finn schools to reconfigure grade levels and take Neary School offline.
trottier-finn-expansion-studies.status: Proposals to study expanding Trottier Middle School and Finn Elementary School were defeated at Special Town Meeting in March 2026. The two articles, which sought up to $500,000 and $324,000 from Free Cash to evaluate reconfiguring district grades and closing Neary School, failed by wide margins after drawing opposition from the School Committee, Select Board, and Advisory Committee. Opponents highlighted site constraints, protected open space next to Finn, and the risk of program reductions, and no subsequent action has been scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted down Article 2 (66-332) and Article 3 (75-332) on March 2, 2026.
Voted 5-0 to recommend defeating both articles, warning that grade reconfigurations would require major additions to avoid cuts to educational programs.
Voted 4-1 to recommend against both study articles ahead of Town Meeting.
Recommended against Article 2 (6-1) and Article 3 (4-3), citing study costs and potential pressure on the FY27 levy limit.
Residents raised questions about site constraints at Finn, study phasing, and whether using Free Cash could trigger a Proposition 2 1/2 operating override.

trottier-school-roof-replacement.name: Trottier Middle School roof replacement
trottier-school-roof-replacement.description: Proposed funding and MSBA grant reimbursement to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School.
trottier-school-roof-replacement.status: Town Meeting approved borrowing up to $8,833,964 in April 2026 to replace the leaking Trottier Middle School roof in partnership with the Massachusetts School Building Authority, which is slated to cover approximately 41 percent of eligible costs. The borrowing authorization was contingent on voter approval of a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion at the May 2026 town election, though the outcome of that vote is not documented in the record. All reviewing town boards and committees unanimously endorsed the project.

positions.detail: Approved Article 15 by a two-thirds majority on April 11, 2026, authorizing $8,833,964 in borrowing contingent on a debt exclusion ballot vote.
Voted 5-0 on March 17, 2026, to recommend Article 15, citing an estimated net town cost of $5.39 million after state reimbursement.
Supported the project and voted 4-0 on March 24, 2026, to approve a voter informational flyer on the roof replacement.
Voted 3-0 on March 18, 2026, to support Article 15 borrowing to address persistent leaking from the school's 1998 roof.
Voted 5-0 on March 16, 2026, to recommend approval of Article 15.

two-family-zoning-amendment.name: Two-family dwelling zoning amendment
two-family-zoning-amendment.description: Proposed zoning bylaw amendment for Town Meeting to eliminate the requirement that a single-family dwelling exist for two years before converting to a two-family home.
two-family-zoning-amendment.status: The proposed zoning amendment to eliminate the two-year waiting period for two-family conversions was scheduled for the October Special Town Meeting after a similar measure failed to win a two-thirds majority in April. The Zoning Board of Appeals and Select Board both backed the article as drafted, but the Advisory Committee voted against recommending it due to concerns about neighborhood density and municipal services. The Planning Board remained undecided after continuing its hearing to evaluate potential floor amendments clarifying district lot sizes. No subsequent proceedings or Town Meeting results have been recorded.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on Oct 7 to advance the article as drafted after approving final warrant revisions on Sep 16.
Voted 5-0 on Sep 24 to support the revised article, following an initial 4-1 vote to recommend approval on Sep 15.
Voted 3-4 on Sep 16 against recommending approval, citing concerns regarding neighborhood density, septic capacity, and school and service impacts.
Continued its public hearing on Sep 28 without taking a formal position while considering a potential floor amendment on district lot sizes.

Supporters favored creating diverse housing options for young families and downsizers, while opponents warned that removing the waiting restriction would invite investor teardowns and dense condominiums.

well-and-septic-regulations.name: Well and septic regulation amendments
well-and-septic-regulations.description: Board of Health regulations governing private well testing, swimming pool setbacks, and subsurface sewage disposal systems.
well-and-septic-regulations.status: The Board of Health unanimously approved amendments to the town's private well and subsurface sewage disposal regulations following a public hearing on July 7, 2026. The new rules separate the roles of septic designers and installers, require physical access for septic repairs, establish a 25-foot well setback from swimming pools, and mandate well testing prior to real estate transfers with an opt-out waiver option. No further board review or action is scheduled.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on July 7, 2026, to approve the amendments as presented following a public hearing.

youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.name: Youth and Family Services Flagg School relocation
youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.description: Office relocation, fit-out, and furniture funding for the Department of Youth and Family Services move to the Flagg School.
youth-services-flagg-school-relocation.status: The Youth Commission unanimously approved allocating up to $5,000 from its revolving donation fund in March 2026 to purchase fire-retardant seating and desks for Youth and Family Services' move to the Flagg School. The department's relocation was targeted for completion by July 1, 2026. No subsequent updates or additional funding requests have come before the commission.

positions.detail: Voted unanimously on March 10, 2026, to spend up to $5,000 from its donation account for compliant replacement furniture.

zoning-act-conformance-amendments.name: State Zoning Act conformance amendments
zoning-act-conformance-amendments.description: Proposed local zoning bylaw amendments aligning Southborough bylaws with state Zoning Act changes regarding non-conforming structures and variances.
zoning-act-conformance-amendments.status: Proposed zoning bylaw amendments to align Southborough rules with recent state Zoning Act revisions are currently being drafted. The Zoning Board of Appeals is working with town counsel to update local standards for variances and pre-existing non-conforming structures. Staff and counsel are preparing draft warrant language for board review ahead of submission for the Annual Town Meeting warrant.

positions.detail: Agreed on Sep 16 to work with town counsel to draft conforming amendments to town bylaws and board policies.

zoning-act-conformance-amendments.next: Annual Town Meeting warrant article submission deadline to the Select Board on December 14, 2026
